subject: Re: Can geom_smooth() show both OLS regressions on a bivariate scatterplot simultaneously?

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Can geom_smooth() show both OLS regressions on a bivariate scatterplot simultaneously?
parts:
I think you'll have to create the lm objects and calculate the predicted values for each one.

If I understand correctly, this is an example of what you don't want:
ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(x=wt, y=mpg)) +
    geom_smooth(aes(x=wt, y=mpg), method="lm", se=FALSE) +
    geom_smooth(aes(x=mpg, y=wt), method="lm", se=FALSE)

What's happening here is that, one geom_smooth is mapping wt to the x-axis, and mpg to the y-axis, and the other is mapping mpg to the x-axis and wt to the y-axis. The way stat_smooth works, it always predicts the y variable based on x, like y ~ x, or possibly some more complex formula, such as y ~ x + I(x^2), but y is always predicted from x.


To predict values yourself, you can use the method which I've written up here:
http://rpubs.com/wch/1409


Applied to mtcars:

# Given a model, predict values of yvar from xvar
# This supports one predictor and one predicted variable.
# xrange: If NULL, determine the x range from the model object. If a vector with
#   two numbers, use those as the min and max of the prediction range.
# samples: Number of samples across the x range.
# ...: Further arguments to be passed to predict()
predictvals <- function(model, xvar, yvar, xrange=NULL, samples=100, ...) {

  # If xrange isn't passed in, determine xrange from the models.
  # Different ways of extracting the x range, depending on model type
  if (is.null(xrange)) {
    if (any(class(model) %in% c("lm", "glm")))
      xrange <- range(model$model[[xvar]])
    else if (any(class(model) %in% "loess"))
      xrange <- range(model$x)
  }

  newdata <- data.frame(x = seq(xrange[1], xrange[2], length.out = samples))
  names(newdata) <- xvar
  newdata[[yvar]] <- predict(model, newdata = newdata, ...)
  newdata
}

# Predict mpg from wt
m1_lm   <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
m1_pred <- predictvals(m1_lm, xvar="wt", yvar="mpg")

# Predict wt from mpg
m2_lm   <- lm(wt ~ mpg, data = mtcars)
m2_pred <- predictvals(m2_lm, xvar="mpg", yvar="wt")

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg)) + geom_point() +
    geom_line(data=m1_pred) +
    geom_line(data=m2_pred)



-Winston






On Thu, Feb 21, 2013 at 8:52 AM, David Holstius <david.h...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi, this is a "cross-post" of an illustrated, reproducible problem/question over at StackExchange:

  <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/14972417>

The gist is that I tried to use something like:

  last_plot() + geom_smooth(aes(y, x), method="lm", se=FALSE)  # as usual
  last_plot() + geom_smooth(aes(x, y), method="lm", se=FALSE)  # <-- this is the problem

... to show both the regression of y on x, and the regression of x on y, in the same figure. 

But the second call to geom_smooth() did not produce the expected behavior. It seems to have correctly computed the slope and intercept with ordinate x and abscissa y, but then failed to invert them for plotting on the figure (which has ordinate y and abscissa x).

Can anyone suggest whether the behavior of geom_smooth() in this case is a bug, a feature, or something else? Perhaps no one else would think of trying this, so it's moot?

Cheers,
David
